refutation.quote: Zeroing the down_proj columns of 1,000 MLP neurons (0.28 %) ranked on 14 real loops by attribution: loops 71 -> 19, cap hits 98 -> 39, tokens/problem 3,870 (-17 %), right 381 (+0.6 points [-3.4, 4.6]). ... Control, 1,000 random neurons: loops 74, cap 104
refutation.note: Same cell the theory covers (cued base, MATH-500, T 0.6 / top-p 1.0, seed 1,000,000; the unedited arm reproduces result-dadeec, which the theory lists under explains). The scope leaves out 'weight-difference cells', meaning the RL-delta cells; a neuron ablation of the base is not one of them, and the advocate made claims on exactly this item (t14, t15). From the mechanism the advocate argued that zeroing a small set of units 'leaves the history feedback in place and loops stay near the 71', and predicted 66 [48, 84] loops and 94 [76, 112] cap hits. Measured: 19 and 39, about a quarter of the loops left, while 1,000 random neurons change nothing. So with the sampler and prompt held fixed, a small specific set of units controls most of the loop hazard. The statement says the hazard is set by history self-similarity and the sampler. The theory could be saved by saying these neurons carry the copy feedback, but that was not what it claimed. These were not counted as strikes only because both readers also predicted high values (55, 60). Also read: result-b30f15 (activations do not predict which sample of a problem fails, within-problem AUROC about 0.51 to 0.57, but that is at T 1.0 and outside scope), result-44b4df and result-5e17a6 (consistent with the theory), knowledge-13cff3.

wins_judgement: Offline total gain is +1.41 nats over 3 computed tests, and almost all of it comes from p3 (+1.59). p3 says the base's first 3,000 characters compress better than RL's on the same problem: 0.633 over 311 pairs, against readers at 0.54 and 0.43. The theory needed this as a premise, and the readers did not foresee it, so the mechanism earned this one as a prediction. But it is descriptive. It shows the base's style is more repetitive. It does not show that repetitiveness causes loops, and the kept pairs (both texts >= 3,000 chars) lean toward hard problems. p2 (+0.58) gives AUROC 0.671 for compressibility of text[:6000] predicting a later rule-A loop (183 kept, 51 positives), against a predicted 0.70 and readers at 0.60. I checked p2.py: it implements the recipe as written (length >= 6,000, loops kept only with onset_A_char >= 7,000, zlib-9 on UTF-8, full pairwise Mann-Whitney with ties at 0.5). The gain is small and confounded across problems: harder or equation-heavy problems give both more compressible openings and more loops, and the rows are not paired within a problem. p4 (-0.755) is the test closest to the claim that RL's prefix helps because it is less self-similar. Within K_own and K_rl, compressibility barely predicts cap hits (0.575 and 0.542, mean 0.558), at the readers' level and below the predicted 0.66. Held-out: t14 and t15 each lose -3.0 (the ablation result above), and t41 is a wash (426.2 measured vs 427 predicted, readers at 426 to 427). Net: the only earned gain is the descriptive premise p3. The causal tests are near the readers (p2) or below them (p4), and the held-out claims drawn from the mechanism missed badly.
rival: The impasse/soundness rival explains the computed numbers about as well. Hard problems produce both long, compressible, enumerative openings and impasses, which accounts for p2's modest cross-problem AUROC. K_rl's 48 finishes against K_own's 23 follow from RL's prefix being correct as readily as from it being less repetitive, and p4's near-chance within-file AUROC fits the rival slightly better. The ablation result (a small unit set removes most loops without changing accuracy) favours neither account cleanly. The two tests the theory itself named as separating were not run. p1 (within-problem: is the capped sample more compressible early than a finishing sample of the same problem?) was not computable, because base-01 F holds one sample per problem. The deletion-of-repeated-lines rerun of K_own (p5, 25 GPU-min) was not run. Either would separate the accounts. A cheap stand-in is p1 on the 4-sample T 1.0 stored rows, or on a multi-seed T 0.6 cell.

novelty.nearest: Duan et al., 'Circular Reasoning: Understanding Self-Reinforcing Loops in Large Reasoning Models': loops are a self-reinforcing trap in which generated content acts as a premise for its own recurrence; 'reasoning impasses trigger the loop onset', which then persists through a self-reinforcing V-shaped attention pattern once the immediate context is repetitive; semantic repetition precedes textual repetition and can be detected early (CUSUM on hidden states). Together with Xu et al. 2206.02369 (repetition probability rises with the number of earlier repeats).
novelty.difference: The paper puts loop onset at a reasoning impasse, which is this theory's rival, and keeps self-reinforcement for persistence. The theory instead says onset hazard grows smoothly with the zlib self-similarity of the whole pre-loop text, and that RL's prefix helps through lower self-similarity rather than through soundness.

import_carries_gain.which: Xu et al. 2206.02369 (repetition probability rises with earlier repetitions) carries p2: 'a more self-similar history predicts a later loop' is that published dose-response measured with zlib instead of repeat counts. That claim gained only +0.58 over readers who had already guessed 0.60. No import carries p3, the largest gain (base openings more compressible than RL's); that is a new empirical fact about these two models. 2610.24715 (top-p lock above threshold) carries the sampler explanations of result-44b4df and result-5e17a6, but those were explained items, not scored gains.

verdict: weak: it survives offline, but nearly all its gain is one descriptive premise (base openings compress better than RL's). Its causal tests are at or below the no-theory readers (p2 +0.58, p4 -0.76), the within-problem and deletion tests that would separate it from the impasse rival were not run, its held-out claims on the neuron ablation (loops 71 -> 19, cap hits 98 -> 39) missed by -3 nats each, and its self-reinforcement core is published (Xu 2022; Duan 2026).
